question: What appearance do dense structures like bone typically have on a standard X-ray image?
explanation: Dense tissues absorb more radiation and prevent it from reaching the film, creating a light or white shadow. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why do air-filled spaces like lungs appear dark on an X-ray image?

options.B: Air offers very little resistance to radiation
options.C: Lungs produce their own black pigment
options.D: Radiation turns black when hitting oxygen

explanation: Low-density areas like air let radiation pass through easily, exposing the image receptor directly to create dark areas. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h1)

question: What are the three main pillars of radiation safety for healthcare workers?
explanation: These three factors directly control and minimize the dose of radiation absorbed by staff during procedures. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h2)

question: Why must female patients of childbearing age be assessed for pregnancy prior to an X-ray?

options.A: To prevent radiation-induced damage to a developing fetus
options.B: To ensure accurate billing records in the hospital
options.C: To calculate the correct contrast dye dosage
options.D: To determine if a wheelchair is required

explanation: Ionizing radiation can harm rapidly dividing cells in embryonic and fetal tissue, leading to structural birth defects. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h2)

question: Which condition is a standard chest X-ray primarily used to identify?
explanation: Chest radiographs clearly show consolidations and fluid collections in lung tissue characteristic of pneumonia. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h3)

question: A patient presents with severe abdominal pain and suspected bowel obstruction. What imaging study is commonly ordered first?
explanation: An upright or supine abdominal X-ray quickly visualizes gas patterns, fluid levels, and bowel distension. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h3)

question: Why must a patient remove metallic jewelry and metal buttons before an X-ray?

options.A: Metal creates dense artifacts that obscure underlying anatomy
options.C: Metal objects interfere with the electrical wiring of the hospital
options.D: Radiographers charge extra fees for metal items

explanation: Metal blocks X-rays completely, leaving bright white spots on the image that hide clinical details. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h4)

question: What is the primary nursing goal of checking the patient's identity prior to an X-ray?

options.A: To prevent wrong-site or wrong-patient imaging errors
options.B: To update the dietary department preferences
options.C: To check if the insurance policy is active
options.D: To speed up the hospital discharge process

explanation: Positive patient identification ensures diagnostic tests match the correct clinical chart and treatment plan. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h4)

question: A patient on a mechanical ventilator requires a portable chest X-ray in the intensive care unit. What is the most important nursing action during this procedure?

options.A: Standing directly in front of the primary beam to comfort the patient
options.B: Disconnecting the ventilator temporarily to stop machine noise
options.C: Administering a heavy sedative before the technician enters
options.D: Ensuring ventilator tubing remains secure and monitoring vital signs

explanation: Critically ill patients require continuous hemodynamic and airway surveillance during diagnostic imaging shifts. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h5)

question: Why do radiographers and nurses ask patients to take a deep breath and hold it during a chest X-ray?

options.A: To expand the lung fields and separate rib spaces
options.B: To prevent the patient from coughing during the exposure
options.C: To lower the patient's heart rate automatically
options.D: To increase blood pressure for a brighter picture

explanation: Maximum inspiration pulls the diaphragm down and spreads the ribs, revealing hidden lung tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h5)

question: What intervention is commonly recommended after an X-ray procedure involving intravenous contrast media?

options.A: Restricting all oral intake for twenty-four hours
options.B: Increasing fluid intake to help clear the contrast
options.C: Keeping the patient flat in bed for a full day

explanation: Adequate hydration accelerates renal excretion of contrast dye, protecting kidney function. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h6)

question: Which action should a nurse take immediately after a patient returns from an X-ray department?

options.A: Discard the patient chart to maintain privacy
options.B: Send the patient immediately for another unrelated test
options.C: Verify patient comfort, restore proper bed alignment, and document the procedure
options.D: Remove all intravenous access lines proactively

explanation: Post-procedure care requires ensuring physical stability, safety, and accurate nursing documentation. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h6)

question: How does pleural effusion typically present on a standard upright chest X-ray?

options.A: Enlargement of the heart silhouette only
options.B: Fracture lines across the lower ribs
options.D: Complete blackness across both lung fields

explanation: Fluid gravity pools in the lowest dependent spaces of the pleural cavity, obscuring the sharp costophrenic angles. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h7)

question: What is a major operational challenge for diagnostic imaging departments in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.B: Too many working machines in every clinic
options.C: Frequent electrical power fluctuations and grid failures
options.D: An excess supply of lead protective aprons

explanation: Unstable power grids disrupt diagnostic services and risk damaging sensitive radiological equipment without proper backup power. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h8)

question: Why is patient education regarding radiation safety especially vital in resource-constrained environments?

options.A: To replace the need for physical lead aprons
options.B: To train patients to operate the X-ray machine themselves
options.C: To alleviate cultural fears and correct misconceptions about medical radiation
options.D: To convince patients to pay higher user fees for tests

explanation: Clear communication helps reduce patient anxiety and improves cooperation during diagnostic imaging procedures. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h8)
